transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep having these thoughts that if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, then someone could get hurt or lose everything. I know, at least part of me knows, that it’s not always rational, but it feels like I’m personally responsible, and I can’t just let it go and move on.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals to try and alleviate these thoughts and feelings of responsibility?

Yes. I reread things over and over—deployment plans, audit logs, access rules, even old messages—to make sure I didn’t miss something. I’ll check door locks too. Sometimes I count through the steps in my head until they feel “safe” or complete.

And if I try to stop before it feels right, I get really panicky. I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else has left because I couldn’t make myself walk away yet.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and feelings of responsibility?

It’s been going on long enough that it feels like a pattern now. The main thing is this responsibility feeling — like if I overlook one setting or one access rule or some warning sign, someone could get hurt or lose everything. Part of me knows that’s not reasonable, but in the moment it feels like it’s on me, and I can’t just move past it.
Do you feel like these rituals, such as rereading or checking, are necessary to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes. In the moment it really feels necessary. If I don’t reread the deployment plan or the logs, or if I don’t check the locks or old messages again, I get this fear that I missed something important and something bad could happen.

Sometimes I’ll go through the steps in my head, counting them until they feel safe or complete. If I try to stop before that, I panic. I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone left because I just couldn’t make myself walk away until it felt done.
Are these thoughts and rituals interfering with your daily life or relationships in any way?

Yes, definitely. It’s affecting work a lot. I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t finish signing off on decisions. I kept getting stuck checking and second-guessing, and by the time I could move forward, it was too late.

My team has started working around me instead of relying on me, which is hard to admit. And outside work, I’ve stopped going to basketball and salsa nights. Those were routines and people that helped keep me grounded, and now I’m kind of losing that too.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific mental acts, such as counting or repeating certain words or phrases, as part of your rituals?

Yes. I count through steps in my head a lot, especially with deployment plans or audit logs. I’ll go back over them again and again until they feel “safe” or complete.

It’s not just work, either. I do it with door locks and even old messages sometimes. If I try to stop before it feels right, I get panicky, so I’ll keep rereading or checking. I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone leaves because I couldn’t stop until it felt done.
Do you have any recurring, intrusive thoughts that aren't related to your work or checking rituals?

Not really separate from that theme, no. It usually comes back to the same kind of thought: that if I miss one setting, one access rule, or one warning sign, someone could get hurt or lose everything.

Part of me knows that’s not reasonable every time, but it still hits me like I’m personally responsible. I can’t just let it go and move on.
Are there any situations or places that you avoid because of these thoughts or feelings of responsibility?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding things where I feel like I might get stuck or let people down.

At work, it got bad enough that I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t finish signing off on decisions. Now my team kind of works around me instead of depending on me, which feels awful.

And outside of work, I’ve stopped going to basketball and salsa nights. I used to really need those routines and those people, but I just haven’t been showing up.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are not about missing something important or checking things?

No, not really outside of that. The thoughts that repeat are mostly the same ones I mentioned — that if I miss some setting, or an access rule, or some warning sign, then someone could get hurt or lose everything.

I know part of me can see it’s not always rational, but in the moment it feels like it’s on me, and I can’t just drop it and move on.
Are there any obsessive thoughts that you have which are not related to preventing harm or making mistakes?

No, I don’t think so. It’s really all tied to that same fear — that I’ll miss a setting or an access rule or some warning sign, and then someone gets hurt or loses everything.

I know part of me can see that it’s not rational, but it still feels like it’s on me, like I’m personally responsible, and I can’t just move past it.
Do you feel like these thoughts of responsibility and fear of missing something are in line with your own values and beliefs, or do they feel alien or inconsistent with who you are?

They don’t feel like me, exactly. I mean, I do care about doing my job right and not putting people at risk, but the way these thoughts hit me feels way beyond that.

It’s like, if I miss one setting or one access rule, my mind goes straight to someone getting hurt or losing everything. Part of me knows that’s not rational, but in the moment it feels like I’m personally responsible, and I can’t just let it go.
Do you feel like these thoughts of responsibility and fear are something that you want to have, or are they unwelcome and something you wish you could stop having?

They’re definitely unwelcome. I don’t want to have them.

I care about being responsible, but this feels different — like my mind jumps straight to, “If I miss one setting or one warning sign, someone could get hurt or lose everything.” I know part of me can see it doesn’t make sense, but it still feels like it’s on me, and I wish I could just stop having that thought and move on.
Do you feel like these thoughts of responsibility and fear are a part of who you are, or do they feel like they are coming from outside of yourself?

They feel like they’re coming from me, but not in a way that feels like who I really am.

I mean, I know I care about being responsible, but these thoughts are way beyond that. It’s like my mind grabs onto one possible missed setting or warning sign and turns it into, “Someone could get hurt, someone could lose everything, and it’ll be my fault.” I don’t want that, and it doesn’t feel like my normal thinking. It just hits me hard and I can’t move past it.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific physical acts, such as tapping or touching, as part of your rituals?

Not really tapping or touching, no. It’s more checking and rereading.

I’ll go back through deployment plans, audit logs, door locks, even old messages again and again. Sometimes I count through the steps in my head until it feels “safe” or complete. And if I stop before it feels done, I get really panicked — I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else left because I couldn’t make myself leave it unfinished.
Do you feel anxious most of the time, even when you're not actively engaged in your rituals or thinking about your responsibilities?

I’m not sure. I mean, I do feel on edge a lot, but I haven’t really separated out whether that’s happening when I’m not thinking about those things.

It feels like the anxiety is tied to the checking and the responsibility thoughts most of the time. Outside of that, I’d have to think about it more.
Have you been experiencing feelings of sadness or hopelessness lately?

I’m not sure I’d call it hopelessness. I do get worn down by all of this, and sometimes I feel pretty low because it feels like I can’t get out of the cycle. But I haven’t really thought of it as sadness in the main sense. It’s more exhaustion and frustration, I guess.
Are there any thoughts that recur and distress you which are not about missing something important or causing harm to others?

Not that I’ve really noticed. Most of the thoughts that bother me seem to come back to missing something, making a mistake, or something bad happening because I didn’t catch it.

I can’t think of a separate kind that keeps coming up, at least not right now.
